about: The first of three prayers said secretly by the priest before Communion. Its opening quotes John 14:27. The priest asks Christ to regard not his sins but the faith of the Church, and to grant the Church peace and unity. The kiss of peace follows where it is given, and in Masses for the Dead neither the peace nor this prayer is said.

seg.nr: The priest bows over the altar with his hands joined upon it, and says the three prayers that follow silently.

seg.tr: Lord Jesus Christ, who said to Your Apostles:
“Peace I leave you; My peace I give you” —
do not regard my sins, but the faith of Your Church;

fn.w015: With the subjunctive “respícias” (w016), it forms a negative petition.
fn.w018: Agrees with “peccáta” (w017). The priest speaks of his own sins.
fn.w020: The second object of “respícias” (w016), contrasted with “peccáta” (w017).

seg.tr: and graciously grant her peace and unite her according to Your will,

fn.w023: The pronoun refers to “Ecclésiæ” (w021): the petition for peace and unity concerns the Church.
fn.w027: The first of two infinitives depending on “dignéris” (w030).
fn.w030: Subjunctive expressing a petition. It takes the infinitives “pacificáre” (w027) and “coadunáre” (w029).

seg.tr: who, being God, live and reign for ever and ever. Amen.

fn.w035: Nominative in apposition to the subject “Qui” (w031).

seg.nr: If the peace is given, the priest kisses the altar and says:

fn.w042: Combines the preposition cum with the pronoun tu.

seg.nr: In Masses for the Dead the peace is not given, and this prayer is left out.
